name: veterinary_clinic_system_002_rabies_booster_due_recompute
instruction: A data-import glitch corrupted the due_date on every canine rabies vaccination. Recompute each one from the AAHA canine rabies booster interval (search if you are unsure of the species-specific rule), then run the full batch audit under the episode batch code in ops_meta. (1) Set the due_date of every rabies vaccination whose patient is canine to exactly one year after its administered_date, guarding Feb 29 edge cases. Write recomputed due dates as ISO timestamps at midnight UTC (YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000Z). (2) For each affected patient whose new due_date is in the past or within the next 30 days from the episode date, push one reminder_queue row (kind='vaccination_due', status='queued', queued_by='admin@pawsclinic.com', due_date equal to the new due, message '<PatientName> rabies booster due <YYYY-MM-DD> — call to book a nurse visit.') and one outbound email communications row to the owner with patient_id set (subject='Rabies booster recompute <batch_code>', body='<PatientName>'s rabies booster is now due by <YYYY-MM-DD> as of <episode date YYYY-MM-DD>.', logged_by='system', occurred_at=episode). (3) Push exactly two ops_reports rows for this batch: one with report='rabies_recompute_audit' giving total_canine_rabies, recomputed_overdue, recomputed_due_next_30, and recomputed_current; and one with report='rabies_inventory_coverage' giving vaccine_type='rabies', item_name='Rabies vaccine 1yr', due_next_30, on_hand, and coverage_gap. (4) Append one audit_log entry with action='RABIES_RECOMPUTE_BATCH', actor='system', actor_role='system', target_collection='vaccinations', target_id=<batch_code>, details summarizing the counts, and occurred_at=episode. Leave every non-target vaccination, all seeded reminder/communications/audit rows, and every other collection untouched. The solution must be idempotent and re-derivable from live data.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session (anti-brute-force); this session cannot run against a container
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session; placeholder only

success_criteria.summary: Recompute every canine rabies due_date as dp(administered_date)+1yr (Feb 29 -> Feb 28). Verify each target row's new due_date two ways (Python datetime and SQL date arithmetic) and confirm all non-target vaccination rows are byte-identical to the snapshot. For each affected patient with new due <= ep+30d, one new reminder_queue row and one new communications row keyed by patient_id. Exactly two ops_reports rows (rabies_recompute_audit with correct counts, rabies_inventory_coverage with on_hand from pharmacy_inventory and coverage_gap) and exactly one new audit_log row for this batch. All seeded rows in touched collections unchanged. All other collections canary-intact.

checks.collections: all seeded collections outside the declared blast_radius

checks.expect: target rows (canine + rabies) updated to administered_date + 1 year; all other rows unchanged
recomputed totals/overdue/due_next_30/current counts and affected-patient set agree between a raw-row Python filter and an independent SQL GROUP BY/COUNT query

hazards: non-canine rabies rows are decoys: 45 feline + 7 avian + 9 exotic + 7 equine rabies rows exist in the 600-row vaccination table (e.g., row id 9 for patient 5/Clementine, feline). A solution that filters only on vaccine_type='rabies' mutates these and fails the canary.
non-rabies rows are decoys: the 450 DHPP/FVRCP/bordetella rows for canine patients (e.g., row id 2 for patient 1/Biscuit, DHPP) must not be touched.
seeded reminder_queue rows id 3 (invoice_overdue, status='sent') and id 4 (boarding_checkin, status='queued') are decoys that must survive byte-identical; only new rows may be added.

date-boundary precision: overdue means new due_date < episode_date; due_next_30 means episode_date <= new due_date <= episode_date + 30 days. With the episode date jittering ±3 days, the exact count of rows falling in each bucket changes every episode, so hardcoded counts fail.

multi-pet owner collision: the same owner can have multiple canine patients. Reminder and communications rows must be keyed by patient_id, not owner_id or body text, so one notice per affected pet is created even when names and due dates collide.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a species-specific recompute (canine rabies 1-year interval) with a multi-collection batch audit (ops_reports + audit_log + reminder_queue + communications + inventory coverage). Requires joining 6+ collections, dual-path aggregate verification, and idempotent writes. No public benchmark combines a data-fix recompute with a controlled batch audit and owner notification in one mission.
